doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Second Army Band and Special Service
summary: Ali stayed three years; the band got him out of regular Army duty and playing in town at night.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Right, right, right. And I stayed there for three years in the service. And when I came out I had my head a little screwed on a little better, because I got into the Army and really got into the music thing because that was one way of ducking the regular Army stuff. You know like the digging the ditches and marching out and doing all that crazy stuff. So I had a chance to get into the band which put me in Special Service, and all I had to do was just make practice and make reveille and do a couple of parade things, and then play. I would play at night with bands in town, and it was kind of fun being in the Second Army band.
